text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: P0 — KV cache eviction storm detected in us-east-1. Continuous-batching timeouts and paging spike. Error rate up ~12% across inference fleet. Runbook: <https://redwood.internal/ops/runbooks/contbatch-kv-eviction>

maria (oncall): oncall here, seeing customer reports for latency and 502s. Swarming now. Paging eng-runtime + SRE.

daniel (sre): looking at infra metrics — node swap/paging increasing, redis/kvcache eviction rate ~18k/s, out-of-memory reclaim logs. p95 latency jumped from 60ms -> 1.8s, p99 ~3.2s.

lee (eng-runtime): I can already see a config delta in config-service: cont_batch.max_batch_tokens was pushed by rollout job 2026-03-15T09:12Z -> value=500000 (intended 50000). That would massively increase per-batch KV entries.

olivia (pm): are we confident that's the root cause? customers complaining that long-context jobs are suddenly much slower.

daniel (sre): correlates perfectly in timeline. After the push, eviction/IO increased and remote paging (disk) ops surged.

lee (eng-runtime): action: we should immediately revert that config and set a hard cap guard at the service layer to prevent future pushes from exceeding safe thresholds. Proposing immediate mitigations: 1) rollback config 2) hotfix to cap max_batch_tokens to 100k 3) temporarily disable cont-batch for the most affected model pool.

maria (oncall): agree. I'll start rollback. @deploy-bot kick rollback.

deploy-bot: rollback job started: cont-batch-config-rollout-rollback-2367001234. Rolling back to version 2026-03-15T08:58Z. Canary nodes first.

support-bot: tagging customer-facing incidents channel and creating preliminary status page entry. Drafting message: "We're investigating increased latency for some generation requests in US-East; working on an internal configuration rollback."

lee (eng-runtime): while rollback is rolling, we should also apply emergency guard via the admin API to avoid a second bad push. Command: 
```
redwoodctl admin set-guard --key cont_batch.max_batch_tokens --max 100000
```
I'll run it now.

lee (eng-runtime): applying guard... response: ok. Guard in place.

deploy-bot: rollback canary results: canary nodes show immediate decrease in eviction rate and p99 latency -> 220ms. Proceeding to full rollout.

olivia (pm): good — can we quantify customer impact (number of requests affected, number of customers)? Support, please pull recent 1h windows.

support-bot: pulled: ~24k unique API keys saw at least one error/latency >1s in the last 45m. Top affected tenants: 5 customers account for 62% of the increased latency volume. Drafting targeted outreach.

maria (oncall): watch for paging backlog during rollback. If disk IO doesn't drop, we may need to drain and restart a few high-IO workers.

daniel (sre): checking worker health. A subset of workers hit high swap; I'm preparing a script to gracefully drain pods with high kvcache eviction. Command to drain: 
```
kubectl annotate pod <pod> meltdown=1 && kubectl rollout restart deployment/cont-batch-worker
```
I'll coordinate with eng-runtime.

lee (eng-runtime): I'm standing by for a quick patch we can hot-patch into runtime to short-circuit continuous batching for sequences > 64 or max_batch_tokens > 20000 until things stabilize. Patch ready: 
```
if (incoming.batch_tokens > config.max_batch_tokens_guard) {
  // fallback to single-request path
  run_without_continuous_batching();
}
```
We can flip a remote flag: `redwoodctl flags set contbatch.fallback_on_guard=true`

maria (oncall): deploy the flag in us-east-1 only. 

lee (eng-runtime): flag set. Observability: contbatch fallback rate reported at ~0.6% — that's expected.

deploy-bot: full rollback complete at +17m. Metrics: kvcache eviction rate down to baseline, remote paging ops drop 86%. p99 latency trending back to normal.

olivia (pm): thanks. Next steps: 1) postmortem, 2) tighten CI checks for config pushes, 3) customer communication. Who's on action items?

maria (oncall): I'll own immediate postmortem draft and timeline.

lee (eng-runtime): I'll own the runtime guard (permanent) and the short-circuit patch for cont-batch. Plan: merge hotfix and schedule canary for tomorrow.

daniel (sre): I'll add infrastructure playbook steps for detecting config deltas that spike eviction and implement an alert that ties config change -> eviction increase within 5m.

support-bot: customer-facing note posted to status page: "Service degradation for some generation requests in US-East resolved. Configuration rollback performed. Affected customers will be contacted with details."

olivia (pm): also prepare a templated outreach for the top 5 customers. We should include root cause, resolution steps, mitigation, and actions to prevent recurrence.

lee (eng-runtime): important follow-up: we found the PR that set the wrong value — it passed config lint but the unit was wrong (tokens vs tens). We'll add stricter schema validation and a deploy-time guard to refuse >100k unless explicitly acknowledged.

maria (oncall): status: incident resolved; monitoring for 2h. Will update postmortem once timeline completed.

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: Incident resolved (P0 -> P1) at 2367002900. Summary: misconfigured cont-batch.max_batch_tokens (500k) caused KV cache blowup -> paging and timeouts. Mitigation: config rollback, guard applied, fallback short-circuit enabled, targeted pod drains. No data loss reported.

olivia (pm): thanks everyone. Please add your notes to the postmortem doc: <https://redwood.internal/ops/postmortems/2367001234>

maria (oncall): closing thread after monitoring window.
